(i) the 3 x TG-AD mice show a differential susceptibility to environmental manipulations; (ii) social isolation did not exacerbate the AD-like symptoms in 3 x TGMice, in contrast to physical exercise; (iii) social isolation did induce a significant reduction in the anxiety-like behavior in female, but not male, mice; (iv) social isolation did affect several behaviors in 3 x TG mice, including the acoustic startle response and performance in the Y maze
social isolation did neither aggravate nor ameliorate the Alzheimer-like symptoms of the triple transgenic mouse, as previously observed with physical activity.
social isolation did have a limited effect on the AD-like symptoms of the 3xTg-AD mouse model.

the 3 x TG-AD model does not seem to be a good tool to investigate the role of environmental factors in the etiopathology of AD.

A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the genetic background of the 3xTg-AD mice, and in particular the amyloid precursor protein (APP) and presenilin (PS) mutations, may be responsible for the behavioral phenotype observed, while the environmental manipulations may have a limited impact.
social isolation does not affect AD-like symptoms in the 3 xTg-AD model.

the 3 x tg-AD model of Alzheimer's disease, although useful to study genetic aspects of the disease, is not a suitable model to study environmental factors that may influence the development of the disease.
The main takeaway from our work is that

the 3 x TG-AD mouse line, despite its genetic predisposition to AD, is not a good model of environmental enrichment, and therefore, it should be considered with caution for future studies on the impact of environmental factors on AD-related traits.

social isolation does not appear to be a risk factor for the development of AD-related traits in the 3 x  Tg-AD model, and thus may not be considered as a major environmental factor in the pathophysiology of AD.
environmental factors can have different impact on AD-like traits depending on the type of manipulation and the specific behavioral measure.
